name: Sick of It All
label: Revelation
lede: Two brothers from Queens, one borrowed basement, a seven-inch that's been repressed in a rainbow of vinyl for almost forty years, and a band that carried New York hardcore onto MTV and around the planet without ever sanding the edges off.

eras.title: Scared to death at the Right Track Inn
eras.text: Lou Koller and Pete Koller built the band in their parents' Queens basement in the summers the folks were away, soaking up metal and hardcore in equal parts. Within a year they'd gone from a nervous opening slot on Long Island to the CBGB Sunday matinees and the third release on a brand-new label called Revelation.

years.cap: Sick of It All · via Discogs
years.h: Sick of It All's first show: the Right Track Inn, Long Island
years.p: [[Craig Setari|3908d895-a1af-42a7-b86b-93a3074057ee]] got Sick of It All on a Right Track Inn bill with [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Straight Ahead|1fd60d7c-dc35-44f5-9162-4113b6ca4a69]] and Crippled Youth. After a month of rehearsal, they closed with a [[Cause for Alarm|1940001f-3270-4d87-9501-eb243d5f9f50]] cover.
years.xp:
Sick of It All didn't feel ready and said so for decades after. The plan was simple: get the unknown songs out of the way, then finish on something the crowd already loved, and let that carry them off stage.

Craig Setari, who booked the gig, would join Sick of It All seven years later and stay for the next three decades.

years.h: Rich Cipriano and Armand Majidi join Sick of It All
years.p: After the first show, Sick of It All's original drummer and bassist were out. [[Rich Cipriano|fe1b3bb1-f4b1-4359-b308-30247a89e9d8]] took bass and [[Armand Majidi|5835deec-ae60-4ac0-888e-5b5e70270d0f]] took the drums, the line-up that made the early records.

years.h: Sick of It All play the CBGB Sunday matinees
years.p: After a self-titled demo, Sick of It All land regular spots on the CBGB hardcore matinees on the Bowery, building a reputation one pit at a time.

years.h: Sick of It All 7" · Revelation No. 3
years.p: Sick of It All's debut: a thousand hand-numbered black copies, with no Rev logo on the A-side art. Its dragon, drawn in the spirit of a Greg Irons tattoo flash sheet, crawls back onto seven of their studio albums.
years.xp: Revelation has kept the record alive ever since: a numbered red second press, 300 black copies for a Gilman Street record convention, a 33 rpm run, a 10th-anniversary repress in 1997, then clear vinyl for Record Store Day 2010 and a string of colors after that.

eras.title: Seven albums on paper, a revolving door in the van
eras.text: A seven-album deal with Relativity put them on the road with everyone from Agnostic Front to Bad Brains to Exodus. The records got bigger while the rhythm section kept changing underneath them, and for one EP the band printed photos of members who were already gone.

years.h: Relativity signs Sick of It All for seven albums
years.p: Lou and Pete Koller go from a Revelation single to a long-term deal, and Sick of It All start opening for [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]], [[Murphy's Law|4a9fae02-7de0-4cb8-97d7-1fd790d9675e]] and, for five East Coast dates, thrash band Exodus.

years.h: Blood, Sweat, and No Tears
years.p: Sick of It All's debut LP, on Relativity. Kerrang! would later say it helped change what the world meant by New York hardcore.
years.xp: Lou Koller was unhappy with how the Injustice System video turned out.

years.h: Sick of It All go west with [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]]
years.p: After headlining runs, Sick of It All support Bad Brains on the Quickness tour with [[Leeway|121193a5-cb8b-4182-968c-8ba607856fa2]], including two weeks on the West Coast.

years.h: Armand Majidi steps away for [[Rest in Pieces|3cb8bd68-6c42-4dea-b0c6-f33c66cc790b]]
years.p: [[Max Capshaw|74d0e618-1149-46b2-898b-7169b7f9819d]] covers Sick of It All's drums while Majidi plays with Rest in Pieces. Majidi is back for a national run with [[D.R.I.|95f6e954-8bed-4f8e-a53e-d155bb6f7ace]], and Lou Koller's later verdict on Capshaw was that he was too young.

years.h: Rich Cipriano and Armand Majidi both leave
years.p: Before an [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]] tour, Sick of It All lose Cipriano and Majidi, and [[Eddie Coen|6c1ec806-8c9e-4a6f-be2f-ae0d940e0f30]] and [[Eric Komst|bba140d0-01c1-4a77-a596-30f376822207]] step in.
years.xp: Coen soon left for the Cycle Sluts from Hell, and Komst was eventually fired.

years.h: We Stand Alone EP pictures members already gone
years.p: Sick of It All picture Eddie Coen and Eric Komst anyway, to show fans the band was still standing. By the next album, Armand Majidi and Rich Cipriano are back.
years.xp: That year Sick of It All toured with [[Sepultura|1d93c839-22e7-4f76-ad84-d27039efc048]], [[Napalm Death|ce7bba8b-026b-4aa6-bddb-f98ed6d595e4]] and Sacred Reich on the New Titans on the Bloc tour.

years.h: Just Look Around
years.p: Sick of It All's second Relativity LP, followed by a spring run through Europe and a winter tour of the continent.

eras.title: Hardcore on Headbangers Ball
eras.text: With Craig Setari on bass the line-up locked in for good, and East West took the band to a major. Scratch the Surface put a New York hardcore video into MTV rotation, something nobody had seen coming, and sent the band to Japan, South America and New Zealand.

years.h: [[Craig Setari|3908d895-a1af-42a7-b86b-93a3074057ee]] finally joins
years.p: Craig Setari, who booked Sick of It All's first show, replaces Rich Cipriano on bass. With Lou and Pete Koller and Armand Majidi, it's the line-up for thirty-plus years.
years.xp: By the end of 1993: shows in Japan, a live album (Live in a World Full of Hate) and a deal with East West.

years.h: Scratch the Surface takes NYHC worldwide
years.p: Sick of It All's first album to chart, debuting at No. 67 in Germany. The title-track video premieres on MTV's Headbangers Ball, and Step Down goes into rotation.
years.xp:
Vice's Mike Hill called it the album that took NYHC worldwide, turning the band into the closest thing hardcore had to a household name. Step Down even turned up on Beavis and Butt-Head.

The touring was relentless: two weeks with [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]], a November run supporting [[Helmet|582fee78-d934-4603-9f5c-1729e0ca36b7]] and [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]], ten shows with [[Black Train Jack|be939900-e334-431e-b85a-c62f4ec3bf60]], then the Americas, Europe, Japan and New Zealand.

years.h: Sick of It All headline over a young [[Korn|ac865b2e-bba8-4f5a-8756-dd40d5e39f46]], then play Warped
years.p: A January to March US headline run with Korn, Orange 9mm and Trial, then a slot on the very first Warped Tour.

years.h: Built to Last on Elektra
years.p: Sick of It All's only album for Elektra, East West's sister label, and home of set staples Us vs. Them, Busted and Good Lookin' Out.
years.xp: The same year Revelation reissued the band's 1987 debut 7" for its tenth birthday.

eras.title: Fat Mike, Slayer and the long road
eras.text: Off the majors and onto NOFX frontman Fat Mike's Fat Wreck Chords, the band stopped chasing anything but the next show. A crowd in Argentina brought Slayer calling, and by the band's 20th birthday a roster of younger bands was lining up to cover them.

years.h: Call to Arms, first for Fat Wreck Chords
years.p: Sick of It All's first album for Fat Mike's label. Earlier in 1999, [[Slayer|bdacc37b-8633-4bf8-9dd5-4662ee651aec]] members catch a Sick of It All show in Argentina, and the band tours with Slayer and [[Meshuggah|cf8b3b8c-118e-4136-8d1d-c37091173413]] later that year.
years.xp: Sick of It All signed to Fat Wreck Chords in 1998 and opened with the Potential for a Fall single.

years.h: Yours Truly, and the cover Lou Koller blames
years.p: Critics were cooler on Sick of It All's 2000 album, though District and Blown Away became fan favorites. Lou Koller later suggested its cover art may have hurt its reception.

years.h: Death to Tyrants on Abacus
years.p: Sick of It All's album for Abacus, a new label under the Century Media umbrella, and one critics heard as proof the band hadn't slowed down.

years.h: Sick of It All's 20th anniversary at B.B. King's
years.p: Sick of It All's 20th anniversary show lands at B.B. King's on 42nd Street in Times Square, a long way from the Right Track Inn on Long Island.

years.h: Our Impact Will Be Felt: everybody covers Sick of It All
years.p: A tribute album with [[Sepultura|1d93c839-22e7-4f76-ad84-d27039efc048]], [[Napalm Death|ce7bba8b-026b-4aa6-bddb-f98ed6d595e4]], [[Rise Against|606bf117-494f-4864-891f-09d63ff6aa4b]], [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]], Bouncing Souls, [[Pennywise|5c210861-2ce2-4be3-9307-bbcfc361cc01]], [[Madball|c9e0a0f5-9f53-4247-a52d-a3f29d975e17]] and more covering Sick of It All songs.

eras.title: Thirty years of the wall of death
eras.text: Now on Century Media, the band marked anniversaries the way they marked everything else: by getting in the van. They played whole albums front to back, re-recorded their own history, and in 2020 the brothers finally put it all in a book.

years.h: Based on a True Story, made in Copenhagen
years.p: Sick of It All's first album for Century Media, recorded with producer Tue Madsen in Copenhagen instead of New York.

years.h: The Last Act of Defiance
years.p: Sick of It All's 2014 album. The same year, at Fun Fun Fun Fest in Austin, they play both Scratch the Surface and Blood, Sweat, and No Tears all the way through.

years.h: Sick of It All turn 30 at Webster Hall
years.p: Sick of It All play a hometown 30th anniversary show at Webster Hall with [[Murphy's Law|4a9fae02-7de0-4cb8-97d7-1fd790d9675e]], in the middle of a world tour for the milestone. When the Smoke Clears, an EP of new songs, follows on November 4.

q: We wanted to show the world what we loved.
years.h: Wake the Sleeping Dragon!
years.p: Sick of It All's 2018 album puts the dragon from their 1987 seven-inch in the title. Around this time Lou Koller pushed back on calling them the Kings of New York hardcore.
years.xp: Lou Koller's preferred word for Sick of It All was ambassadors, not kings. It fit a group that had spent thirty years bringing New York hardcore to Brazil, Japan and German festival fields.

years.h: Lou and Pete Koller publish their memoir
years.p: With touring shut down, Lou and Pete Koller publish The Blood and Sweat: The Story of Sick of It All's Koller Brothers. Decibel called it one of the best books ever written about hardcore.

eras.title: The last fight
eras.text: Forty years in, the band's hardest stretch had nothing to do with labels or line-ups. First Pete Koller sat out a 2022 tour for surgery, then Lou Koller's esophageal cancer pulled them off the road, the scene he helped build rallied around him, and in the band's 40th year he died.

years.h: Sick of It All tour Europe without Pete Koller
years.p: Pete Koller sits out Sick of It All's 2022 European tour to have surgery for a hernia, as Blabbermouth and Wikipedia report. Craig Silverman fills in on guitar, and Pete is back afterward.

years.h: Lou Koller's cancer diagnosis cancels Sick of It All's Europe dates
years.p: Lou Koller announces he's been diagnosed with esophageal cancer; Rolling Stone reported it as a tumor diagnosis. He starts treatment that summer, and Sick of It All's July European dates are cancelled.

years.h: The scene plays a benefit for Lou Koller
years.p: [[Life of Agony|d6ff259a-bbb6-4454-8503-80151da5f2db]], [[Municipal Waste|b5a31e9b-1fa2-45f9-91f5-b3a25fb38038]], [[Crown of Thornz|e7b3e015-81fa-4180-aa7b-7bfcf821209d]] and [[Vision of Disorder|618a18b1-dec3-4c4a-813b-988d9c065722]] play a benefit show for the Sick of It All singer.

years.h: Lou Koller's cancer returns months after he's declared free
years.p: Lou Koller announced in May 2025 that he was officially cancer free. In late September he tells fans the cancer has come back.
years.xp: In between, in August, Craig Setari said new Sick of It All music was in the works, with shows planned for 2026.

years.src: Blabbermouth · Arrow Lords of Metal · Wikipedia
years.h: Lou Koller's treatment reaches a stalemate
years.p: Lou Koller describes his treatment as at a stalemate, with the tumors neither growing nor shrinking. Pete Koller says his brother lost 70 pounds and was put on a feeding tube, as Blabbermouth reported.

years.cap: Sick of It All · via Discogs
years.h: Lou Koller dies in Sick of It All's 40th year
years.p: Lou Koller died on July 24 in hospice care in Matawan, New Jersey, after a two-year fight with esophageal cancer. He is survived by his wife Melissa, his daughter and his brother Pete.
years.xp: The band announced it to what they called their worldwide hardcore family.

years.h: Pete Koller: Lou asked Sick of It All to keep going
years.p: In an Instagram video, Pete Koller says his brother Lou wanted Sick of It All to continue after him, and that the band is working out how to honor that.
